summary.text: A 19-year-old female presented with sore throat, right-sided jaw pain and a right neck mass present for 4 months. Neck ultrasound showed a markedly vascular mass at the right carotid sheath, and MRI showed an enhancing right carotid space mass with carotid and jugular vein splaying, suggesting a vagal paraganglioma with schwannoma less likely.

Enlarged jugular chain and retropharyngeal nodes were felt likely reactive, urinary catecholamines were normal and abdominal MRI showed no adrenal or extra-adrenal paraganglioma. At surgery hypervascular solid nodes were seen in levels 2 and 3, and frozen section showed paraganglioma cells in them, confirming malignancy.

The malignant tumour was resected with sacrifice of cranial nerves X and XII, reconstructed by ansa cervicalis transfer and a greater auricular nerve graft. Histopathology showed malignant VPG in 4 of 13 level 2 and 3 nodes with involved skull base margins. Post-operative radiotherapy followed, with referral for genetic testing and family counselling.

summary.text: A 54-year-old male presented with left jaw swelling four years after resection of a primary left mandibular ameloblastoma. CT suggested soft tissue recurrence lateral to the mandible and an enlarged left level 1b submandibular node with heterogeneous internal density, felt most likely reactive; surgery was planned to excise the local recurrence.

He underwent excision of the soft tissue mass with en bloc node resection. Histology showed recurrent ameloblastoma in the soft tissue and metastatic ameloblastoma within the submandibular lymph node. A second stage selective neck dissection of levels 1 to 3 found no malignancy in 23 nodes.
Radiation therapy was discussed but not undertaken. He is under annual surveillance at the treating centre and has no evidence of recurrence 18 months after revision surgery.

summary.text: A 72-year-old female presented with right-sided neck swelling 1 year after craniofacial resection of a Hyams grade 2 olfactory neuroblastoma, which had initially presented with 6 months of right nasal obstruction, anosmia and facial swelling. Her initial MRI had shown the primary tumour as a large, destructive mass in the right maxillary sinus. She received adjuvant radiotherapy to the primary site.

Restaging CT of the neck at 12 months showed hyperenhancing cervical lymphadenopathy. Ultrasound showed hypervascular right levels 1B and 2 nodes, and ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration confirmed metastatic olfactory neuroblastoma. She had a right comprehensive neck dissection followed by radiotherapy to the right neck.

Follow-up PET at 3 months demonstrated T10 and left humerus metastases, from which she was asymptomatic, and local radiotherapy was given to the T10 metastasis. The bony metastases progressed within the following year and the patient subsequently died.

evidence.quote: right-sided neck swelling 1 year after craniofacial resection
Restaging CT scan of the neck at 12 months

ambiguities.issue: The restaging CT at 12 months and the presentation with neck swelling 1 year after craniofacial resection are not stated to be the same encounter.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not merge the CT and the presentation into one event or anchor the 12 months to resection.

evidence.quote: the bony metastases progressed within the following year and the patient subsequently died

ambiguities.issue: The anchor of the following year is not named, and no date or interval of death is given.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign a date or interval to progression or death.

evidence.quote: Follow-up positron emission tomography (PET) at 3 months demonstrated T10 and left humerus metastases

ambiguities.issue: The bone metastases are reported from follow-up PET; no biopsy or other confirmation is described, and the 3 months has no named anchor.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not treat the bone metastases as pathologically confirmed or anchor the 3 months to a specific treatment.
